caption:
You can still make Veo videos for free: Google Flow gives every account 50 credits a day, and a Veo 3.1 Lite clip costs 10.
The Gemini app now needs a paid plan for video, so Flow is the free route.
The full step-by-step guide with prompts is on neurafeedai.com.

What would you make with 5 free clips a day?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Google Flow Help · Photo: Google
threads_text: Free Veo still exists, just not where most people look. The Gemini app needs a paid plan for video now, but Google Flow gives everyone 50 credits a day and a Veo 3.1 Lite clip costs 10. Have you tried Flow yet?

slides.headline: How to use *Veo for free*: 5 AI video clips a day in Google Flow

slides.heading: 1. Open *Flow*, not Gemini
paras: Video in the Gemini app now needs a paid Google AI plan.
Flow is free for adults in supported countries: open labs.google/fx/tools/flow in Chrome or Edge and sign in.

slides.heading: 2. Pick *Veo 3.1 Lite*
paras: Every account gets 50 credits a day. A Veo 3.1 Lite clip of 4, 6 or 8 seconds at 720p costs 10.
That is 5 clips a day. Credits do not roll over.

slides.heading: 3. Write it like a *shot*
paras: Say who, where, what moves and how the camera moves.
One clear action per clip works better than a whole story.
slides.prompt: Slow push-in on a golden retriever sitting on a rainy city sidewalk at night, shop lights reflecting in puddles, the dog tilts its head toward the camera. Quiet rain sounds.

slides.heading: 4. Start from a *photo*
paras: Under Video, choose Frames and add a start frame, or an end frame too, to animate your own picture.
Failed clips get their credits back within an hour.

slides.hook: Follow for free ways to use the AI tools everyone else is paying for.

site_article.headline: How to use Veo for free: 5 clips a day in Google Flow
site_article.dek: The Gemini app now needs a paid plan for video, but Google Flow still gives every account 50 daily credits. Here is how to spend them on Veo 3.1 Lite, with prompts to copy.
site_article.summary: Google Flow gives every eligible account 50 free credits a day, and a Veo 3.1 Lite clip of 4, 6 or 8 seconds at 720p costs 10 credits. Video in the Gemini app itself requires a Google AI plan.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Veo for free in Google Flow (50 daily credits)
site_article.seo_description: How to use Veo for free: open Google Flow, spend 50 daily credits on Veo 3.1 Lite clips, animate a photo with Frames, plus 4 prompts and the real limits.
site_article.answer_summary: Open Google Flow at labs.google/fx/tools/flow in Chrome or Edge, sign in, and pick Veo 3.1 Lite. Every account gets 50 credits a day and each Lite clip costs 10, so you can make about five free clips daily.
site_article.hero_alt: Google's promotional graphic for its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model.

paragraphs.text: If you want to know how to use Veo for free, go to Google Flow, not the Gemini app. Flow gives every account without a subscription basic video generation and 50 credits a day, and a Veo 3.1 Lite clip costs 10 of them. That works out to five short clips a day at no cost.

The Gemini app changed this year. Google's help center says video in the app now uses Gemini Omni Flash, which replaced Veo 3.1 there, and the limits page lists video generation as unavailable without a Google AI plan. So the free path to Veo runs through Flow.
Before you start

Flow requires you to be 18 or older, with your age verified through your Google account, and to live in a supported country. Google says to use a Chromium browser such as Chrome or Edge. Free users may find video generation unavailable at busy times, roughly 2 to 5 PM UTC.
How to use Veo for free in Flow, step by step

paragraphs.title: 1. Open Flow and sign in
paragraphs.text: Go to labs.google/fx/tools/flow in Chrome or Edge and sign in with your Google account. Your 50 daily credits refresh the day after your first generation, and unused credits do not carry over, so there is no point saving them.

paragraphs.title: 2. Choose Veo 3.1 Lite in the settings
paragraphs.text: In the prompt box you can set the model, the aspect ratio, the number of outputs and the clip length. Pick Veo 3.1 Lite and a length of 4, 6 or 8 seconds. Lite clips are 720p. Keep the number of outputs at one if you want your credits to last.

paragraphs.title: 3. Type a prompt and generate
paragraphs.text: Describe one shot, not a whole film. Credits are taken when a generation starts and refunded within an hour if it fails or is blocked by a safety filter. If audio fails, Flow shows an Audio Generation Failed message and refunds those credits too. There is also a setting to return silent videos.

paragraphs.title: 4. Animate your own photo with Frames
paragraphs.text: Under Video, choose Frames, then add a start frame. You can also add an end frame and let the model fill the motion in between. Veo 3.1 Lite supports a first frame or a first and last frame.

paragraphs.title: 5. Use Ingredients to keep a character
paragraphs.text: Under Video, choose Ingredients and add images by dragging them in, typing @ and the asset name, or using Add and then Upload media. With Veo 3.1 Lite, ingredients only work for 8 second clips.

Flow's help center lists these costs: Veo 3.1 Lite is 10 credits per clip for everyone. Omni Flash 1.2 is also open to free users, for clips up to 10 seconds, at 1 credit per second at 360p or 3 per second at 720p. Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Quality and Omni Flash 1.1 are being retired on December 5, 2026.
Veo prompts to copy

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A product shot
paragraphs.text: Slow orbit around a [product] on a wooden table by a window, soft morning light, shallow depth of field, steam rising from a coffee cup in the background.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A street scene with sound
paragraphs.text: Handheld shot walking down a busy [city] street market at dusk, vendors calling out, string lights turning on, the camera stops at a fruit stall. Natural crowd sounds.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Bring a photo to life (use with Frames)
paragraphs.text: The person in the photo slowly turns toward the camera and smiles, a light breeze moves their hair, the background stays still.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 4: A simple explainer shot
paragraphs.text: Top-down shot of hands drawing a [simple diagram] on white paper with a black marker, one line at a time, clean and well lit.
Five clips a day goes fast. Test a new idea with a 4 second clip first, then spend credits on an 8 second version once the shot looks right.
What free users do not get

Extending clips, 15 second Omni clips and free upscaling to 1080p are for subscribers. Veo 3.1 Lite itself has no extend or video-to-video option. Paid plans add monthly Flow credits on top of the daily 50: 200 on Google AI Plus at $4.99 a month, 1,000 on AI Pro at $19.99, and 10,000 or 25,000 on AI Ultra, which starts at $99.99.

Every Flow video carries an invisible SynthID watermark. A visible watermark is an optional setting in the menu under your profile picture, except in India, South Korea and Vietnam, where it stays on for anyone below the top Ultra tier. Engadget also noted that SynthID is added to all Omni videos.
If you were hoping to use Veo for free through the Gemini API instead, Google's pricing page lists the Veo 3 and 3.1 free tier as not available. The API charges per second of video.

Flow is the best free deal Google offers for AI video right now, but it is built around credits, and five Lite clips a day is enough to learn the tool, not to make a long project. Busy hours can block free users entirely. If you need longer clips, extensions or sharper output, that is where the paid plans start to make sense.
